chunks.arabic_text: ١ - يُونُسُ بْنُ ظِبْيَانَ، كُوفِيٌّ. غَالٍ، كَاذِبٌ وَوَّاعٌ لِلْحَدِيثِ. رَوَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ). لَا يُلْتَفَتُ إِلَى حَدِيثِهِ.

translations.en: 1 – Yūnus b. Zhabyan, Kufan. A ghālī, a liar and a fabricator of ḥadīth. He narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him). His ḥadīth are not turned to.

en.summary: Yūnus ibn Ḍibyān, a Kufan narrator, is characterized in al-Ghadā'irī's *Kitāb al-Duʿafāʾ* as a *ghālī* (extremist) and a liar, leading scholars to largely disregard his narrations despite his transmission from Imām al-Jāfiḍ. His status as a *ghālī* highlights the critical Shia concern with theological deviations in the chain of transmission, particularly regarding the divinity or attributes of the Imams. This entry serves as a key example of how biographical evaluation (*ʿilm al-rijāl*) prioritizes doctrinal fidelity alongside textual accuracy.
en.seo_question: Who is Yūnus ibn Ḍibyān and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.يُونُسُ بْنُ ظِبْيَانَ: Yūnus ibn Ḍibyān, the narrator being described
key_terms.غَالٍ: Ghālī, an extremist who exaggerates the status of the Imams
key_terms.وَّاعٌ: Wāʿi, a fabricator or one who invents narrations
key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh, referring to Imam al-Jāfiḍ (peace be upon him)
key_terms.لَا يُلْتَفَتُ: Lā yul tafatu, not relied upon or disregarded
